readout_other: Cue-induced craving visual analog scale; urine toxicology (GC-MS); HAM-D; C-SSRS; SHAPS; Neuro-QOL; safety MRI
direction_notes: Cue-induced methamphetamine craving fell by about 75% after the first active block and was 0/10 after later blocks and at all follow-ups to day 90; no neural readout of direction.
safety_notes: No unexpected or FUS-procedure-related adverse events through day 90; safety MRIs showed no edema or hemorrhage.

exposures.label: Bilateral NAc FUS, four 5-min active blocks

timing.protocol_description: Four 5-min (300 s) blocks of active FUS (eight subspots alternated; 70-100 W; duty cycle 3.3% per subspot; 100 repetitions; repetition time 3 s; pulse duration 100 ms) to bilateral NAc, 20 min of active FUS in total, after one 5-min zero-energy block.

source_quotes.n_subjects: As this case report includes a single participant with MUD, these findings could not be statistically quantified and these results must be replicated in larger randomized, sham-controlled trials before definitive conclusions regarding the utility of FUS for MUD can be made.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: The participant received a 20-min session of low-intensity FUS (220 kHz) neuromodulation and completed follow-up visits 1-, 7-, 30-, 60-, and 90-days postprocedure.

flags.reason: Paper gives a repetition time of 3 s, recorded as 0.333 Hz (unit conversion); PRF not stated directly. Duty cycle is stated 'per subspot' with eight subspots alternated.
2 MPa is an estimate at 100 W; the paper does not say whether it is free-field or in situ.
Each 5-min block of 100 repetitions at 3 s; 20 min of active FUS in total; 70-100 W varied across blocks.
Participant was not told the order of zero-energy and active blocks; no blinding of investigators described. Recorded as single.
